title: Ephemeral vs Root Key Hygiene: rollout of per-scope ephemeral keys, enforced naming, and admin graceflow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Replace ad-hoc long-lived service/admin tokens with a two-tier credential model: short-lived per-scope ephemeral service keys for workloads and tightly-scoped admin keys with enforced naming, expiry and emergency graceflow. The goal is to reduce blast radius from key leakage, improve audit signal for credential use, and make rotations predictable and automatable while preserving developer ergonomics for CI and platform teams.
comments: 2026-02-14 - Created ticket after post-mortem on INC-2026-02: exposed long-lived service key in CI logs. Initial scoped design sketched in Confluence.
2026-02-21 - Security review sync: agreed on two-tier model (ephemeral service keys + hardened admin keys). Decided not to force immediate deletion of existing keys; introduce migration shims.
2026-02-28 - Proto implemented: gateway accepts ephemeral X-Redwood-Ephemeral header and validates short TTL JWT issued by KMS. See PR #5238 for runtime changes.
2026-03-05 - Design feedback from PM (Maya Chen): require human-review flag and graceflow channel for emergency admin revokes to avoid production outages.
2026-03-10 - Infra approves IAM naming convention and adds server-side enforcement in auth-proxy. Infra PR #149 landed; feature branch deployed to staging.
2026-03-12 - Observability: added credential-usage dashboard panels to surface hourly token issuance and orphaned tokens. Early staging test shows 12% of keys are unused for >30 days.
2026-03-13 - This ticket moved to In Review: implementation artifacts consolidated; requesting Security sign-off and a short rollout plan for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime validates ephemeral keys and falls back to legacy keys only when migration-shim header present
Auth proxy rejects admin keys that do not follow naming convention (env:role:scope:expiryhash) with clear error code
Automated rotation job issues new ephemeral keys via KMS and records rotation events to audit-log S3, retention 2 years
Console highlights expired/unused keys and provides one-click rotate and revoke actions for owners
Migration path documented and runbook exists for emergency revoke with human-review channel and rollback steps
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (staging): add auth-proxy enforcement rule + ephemeral header acceptance in runtime (done, branch: feature/ephemeral-shim)
Phase 2 (canary): deploy to 10% of hosted traffic; emit credential-usage metrics and error rates to SLO dashboard
Phase 3 (migration): enable naming enforcement in read-only mode for one week, notify owners via console and email
Phase 4 (enforce): enable hard reject for non-compliant admin keys and begin automatic graceflow channel for emergency exceptions
Phase 5 (dedicated/private): release a configuration toggle for Dedicated/Private customers and provide a migration checklist and support windows
risks: Developer friction: CI systems that expect long-lived tokens may break. Mitigation: provide short-lived CI integration helper and docs.
False positives: overly-strict naming enforcement could reject valid keys. Mitigation: two-week read-only window and admins CLI to mark exceptions.
Operational outage: emergency rotation could cause rolling auth failures. Mitigation: graceflow human-review and staged rollout with canary traffic.
Telemetry gaps: existing audit logs may not capture key issuance events at sufficient granularity. Mitigation: add explicit issuance events and correlate with request logs.
